predecessors.name: United States of America
predecessors.text: the New Hampshire Grants, claimed by both New Hampshire and New York

successors.name: United States of America
successors.text: Vermont's last shape, admitted to the Union on 4 March 1791

ledger.x: 15 January 1777: Vermont declares independence as the Republic of New Connecticut.
2 June 1777: the Republic of New Connecticut is renamed Vermont.
1781: Vermont claims the 'East Union' and 'West Union'.
4 March 1791: Vermont joins the United States.

wars.name: New Hampshire Grants dispute
wars.outcome: Settled without a territorial change: New York's legislature consented to Vermont's statehood on 6 March 1790 and the commissioners concluded the talks on 7 October 1790, Vermont paying '$30,000'; Vermont entered the Union on 4 March 1791.

wars.name: Haldimand negotiations
wars.outcome: No change: after the 1780 Royalton raid, Ethan Allen led secret talks with Frederick Haldimand about returning Vermont to British rule; 'The British accepted the republic's reunion terms', and Vermont ended the talks after Yorktown (1781).

certainty.note: The frontiers of the Grants were claims of New Hampshire and New York until the 1790 settlement; the Connecticut River on the east is the firmest line.
